reference.name: Release tag name validation error shows an internal field key
reference.summary: On New Release, an invalid, empty or too-long tag name shows an error that names the field with the internal key form.TagName instead of the visible 'Tag name' label.
reference.expected: The tag name validation error names the Tag name field in readable language.
reference.actual: Entering tagcreate-invalid..name as the tag name and clicking Create Tag Only showed 'form.TagName must be a well-formed Git reference name.' Empty and over-long tag names show the same raw key.
reproSteps: Open a repository's New Release page.
Enter tagcreate-invalid..name as the tag name and click Create Tag Only (or Publish Release).

knownHits.reason: Matches the tag-validation message exposing form.TagName instead of the readable field label.

reference.name: Tag search treats underscores and percent signs as wildcards
reference.summary: The Tags page search passes the query to the database LIKE pattern unescaped, so '_' matches any single character and '%' matches anything. Searching a_b also lists a-b and axb tags, v1_0_0 finds v1.0.0, and searching % or _ lists every tag.
reference.expected: Tag search treats '_' and '%' as literal characters, so it only lists tags whose names contain them.
reference.actual: With tags rel-a_b, rel-a-b and rel-axb, searching a_b listed all three ('3 Tags'), while a-b listed only rel-a-b. Searching % or _ listed all 5 tags, including ones with no percent sign or underscore. On harbor-handbook, v1_0_0 returned v1.0.0.
reproSteps: In a repository, create tags rel-a_b, rel-a-b and rel-axb (New Release > Create Tag Only).
Open the repository's Tags page, search for a_b and note the results.
Search for % and check whether tags without a percent sign are listed.

knownHits.reason: Matches Tags search interpreting percent signs and underscores as wildcards rather than literal characters.

reference.name: Tags page uses plural grammar when one tag is listed
reference.summary: A repository with one tag displays the heading `1 Tags` while the nearby tab correctly displays `1 Tag`.
reference.expected: The tag heading should use singular grammar when exactly one tag exists.
reference.actual: A repository with one tag displays the heading `1 Tags` while the nearby tab correctly displays `1 Tag`.
reproSteps: Open an authenticated repository that contains exactly one tag.
Observe that the list heading says `1 Tags` while the nearby tab says `1 Tag`.

knownHits.reason: Matches the single-tag list heading saying 1 Tags while the nearby tab correctly says 1 Tag.

reference.name: Mobile tag row clips release and delete actions that scrolling cannot reveal
reference.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, the tag row clips New Release and leaves Delete Tag outside the visible row; ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page does not expose the actions.
reference.expected: Authorized tag-row actions remain accessible through the rendered UI at a narrow viewport, whether by responsive layout or ordinary scrolling.
reference.actual: The v1.0.0 row displays only a clipped beginning of New Release and leaves Delete Tag offscreen. Horizontal scrolling attempts on the row and page do not reveal the hidden controls.
reproSteps: Sign in with code-write and release-write access to an unarchived repository. Use a tag without an associated published release so New Release and Delete Tag apply; the recorded run used the seeded v1.0.0 tag.
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open the repository Tags page and search for the tag. The recorded path was /eval/harbor-handbook/tags?q=v1.0.0.
Inspect the tag action row: only the beginning of New Release is visible and Delete Tag is offscreen.
Attempt ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page. Observe that the actions remain clipped or hidden; no tag deletion or release creation is necessary to inspect the defect.

knownHits.reason: Matches mobile tag rows clipping New Release and making Delete Tag unreachable even through horizontal scrolling.
